messages:
sara: Heads-up — we're planning to bring up the Horizon-7B fork for evals. LICENSE.md mentions an attribution clause and a 'no redistribution of weights' note. Can legal confirm whether we can quantize and serve this on Redwood-hosted or Dedicated?

aj (Infra): Quick skim: LICENSE.md says 'inference use allowed for commercial use' in one section, but there's a separate 'weights' paragraph that says weights are non-redistributable. Also author wants a specific attribution string in product UI.

mike (Eng-ML): We're planning 4-bit quant experiments and to host on Dedicated + Redwood-hosted API for internal benchmarks. Does quantized checkpoint count as a derivative? The license says 'no derivative works without permission'.

claire (Legal): Short answer: possibly. "Derivative works" wording is the pivot here. Quantization can be considered a transformation that creates a derivative checkpoint. Some licensors explicitly permit inference-optimized variants; many do not. Until we get explicit permission, do NOT publish or ship quantized weights.

sara: So internal evals are fine but production-hosted offerings may be blocked unless we get permission?

claire (Legal): Right. Internal/intra-company evals are typically OK. Hosted API is riskier because it looks like a commercial service backed by our copies of the weights. For Dedicated where the customer provides the weights (BYOW), it's safer — we're not redistributing. If we supply the weights to customers, that's redistribution.

aj (Infra): Practical mitigation: implement BYOW for Dedicated and Private deployments (customers upload their own checkpoint). For hosted API, we should request an explicit license addendum or publisher agreement that allows inference-serving and quantized derivatives.

mike (Eng-ML): Also: embeddings — we'll run embedding benchmarks and return vectors. Any special restrictions there?

claire (Legal): If the license permits inference/commercial use, embeddings are usually fine. Rarely, a licensor restricts "use for competitive services" or output use; if present, it's spelled out. I'll review the exact text and flag any output-use clauses.

sara: They require an attribution snippet in product UI: exact wording included in LICENSE.md. Does that mean we must show a banner or can it be in an 'About' modal?

claire (Legal): Most licensors accept a link + attribution in documentation or an 'About model' modal, but some insist on prominent in-product credit. We'll ask for clarification. I'll draft a standard attribution snippet we can use while we wait.

license-bot: Automated note — created ticket LEG-214 to request explicit permission from Horizon authors for hosting and derivative checkpoints. Assigned to claire.

mike (Eng-ML): For internal reproducibility we want to keep eval outputs and logs. Are generated outputs restricted?

claire (Legal): Generated outputs are normally fine and belong to the service user, but some models have unusual clauses. I'll include a check for 'output ownership' language when I review.

sara: Action items: 1) claire to request permission for hosting + quantization (LEG-214) 2) aj to implement BYOW flow and docs 3) mike to continue internal quant experiments but DO NOT check-in quantized artifacts to any repo or S3 path that could be downloaded 4) legal to confirm attribution wording and output ownership.

claire (Legal): Agreed. I'll ping upstream today; expect 3-5 business days for response. If denied, fallback = BYOW + a how-to to quantize locally.

aj (Infra): I'll add a BYOW note to infra onboarding and put a short checklist: "do not accept/upload vendor weights without legal sign-off".

mike (Eng-ML): Internal-only quant snippet (for infra/security review — do not publish):
```
python quantize.py --model-path /mnt/horizon/checkpoint --bits 4 --out /tmp/hz-4bit.pt
```

sara: :thumbsup: Thanks all. I'll add this to the model-onboarding checklist and tag LEG-214.

claire (Legal): One more note — export controls: verify model origin. If the upstream is subject to export restrictions, additional review may be required. I'm adding that to LEG-214.

license-bot: LEG-214 updated with export-control flag.

aj (Infra): noted. Will hold off on any public deployments until legal clears.

mike (Eng-ML): ok, continuing internal benching. Will post a short results summary in #eng-ml when we have numbers.
